defer stacks a call to run only when the surrounding function returns, LIFO order. The idiomatic pattern is: open a resource, check the error, and immediately follow with the defer that closes it — that guarantees cleanup no matter how many return paths the function has

notesMap.2026-07-31:
When a closure references a variable from its enclosing scope, Go's escape analysis detects that and allocates the variable on the heap instead of the stack. It's only garbage-collected once there's no live reference to it left — typically when the closure using it also goes out of scope
